title: ROB-GD: Grover search over robust shadow scores, O(2^{n/2} n^2 log^2 n) work, 99/100 tolerance of adaptively placed dephased copies, O(n) copies and qubits

claims.statement: For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the ROB-GD algorithm (robust shadow scores plus Grover search) with the single parameter rule of proof.md Section 4 (J = max(1, n-2), r1 = 200 bitlength(16(J+1) 10^6), Q = 2^19 (n+4) copies, q = 16 angle bits, p = q + 1 + bitlength(n) phase bits, cosine table of precision 2^-22, threshold 1/400, K = floor(2^{n/2}), k_G = floor(785K/1000) Grover iterations, at most three repetitions) has worst-case total work T(N,s) = O(2^{n/2} n^2 log2^2 n) in the challenge cost model (all classical bit operations, circuit generation, gates, measurements, initialisation, table construction, address charge ceil(log2(M+2)) = O(log n) per counted operation, where M = O(n^2) is the number of allocated bits plus qubits; each source copy costs n+1; proof.md Section 7: at most 3 repetitions of at most 0.785 * 2^{n/2} Grover iterations, each with an oracle of O(Q n log n) gates, plus O(n^3 log^2 n) for acquisition and label estimation), i.e. uniform envelope B_T(n) = 2^{n/2} n^2 (log2 n)^2, whose growth index is exactly 1. This holds on every execution branch, for the clean problem and for every adversary of the error model of the fifth claim, jointly with the other three resource bounds and full-secret success probability at least 49/64 (> 2/3) of the same algorithm and configuration. All constants are absolute (independent of N, s, the adversary and all outcomes).

For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the ROB-GD algorithm (robust shadow scores plus Grover search) with the single parameter rule of proof.md Section 4 (J = max(1, n-2), r1 = 200 bitlength(16(J+1) 10^6), Q = 2^19 (n+4) copies, q = 16 angle bits, p = q + 1 + bitlength(n) phase bits, cosine table of precision 2^-22, threshold 1/400, K = floor(2^{n/2}), k_G = floor(785K/1000) Grover iterations, at most three repetitions) has worst-case peak classical space S_C(N,s) = O(n^2) bits (Q records of n+p+4 bits, the 2^16-entry cosine table and its constant-size construction workspace, an O(n log log n + n)-bit label-estimation and long-division workspace, the O(n)-bit search controller (K, k_G, counters, current constants, threshold, one stored gate description); explicitly S_C <= 2^19 (n+4)(n+p+4) + 3 * 2^19 + O(n log log n + n)), i.e. envelope B_C(n) = n^2, whose growth index is exactly 0. This holds on every execution branch, for the clean problem and for every adversary of the error model of the fifth claim, jointly with the other three resource bounds and full-secret success probability at least 49/64 (> 2/3) of the same algorithm and configuration. All constants are absolute (independent of N, s, the adversary and all outcomes).

For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the ROB-GD algorithm (robust shadow scores plus Grover search) with the single parameter rule of proof.md Section 4 (J = max(1, n-2), r1 = 200 bitlength(16(J+1) 10^6), Q = 2^19 (n+4) copies, q = 16 angle bits, p = q + 1 + bitlength(n) phase bits, cosine table of precision 2^-22, threshold 1/400, K = floor(2^{n/2}), k_G = floor(785K/1000) Grover iterations, at most three repetitions) has worst-case peak quantum space S_Q(N,s) = O(n) qubits (acquisition: one held (n+1)-qubit source copy, one test control, O(n) adder ancillas and one fair-bit qubit, released after each copy; search: n candidate qubits, O(log n) qubits for the phase accumulator, table index, table word and score accumulator, O(n) comparator and diffusion ancillas), i.e. envelope B_Q(n) = n, whose growth index is exactly 0. This holds on every execution branch, for the clean problem and for every adversary of the error model of the fifth claim, jointly with the other three resource bounds and full-secret success probability at least 49/64 (> 2/3) of the same algorithm and configuration. All constants are absolute (independent of N, s, the adversary and all outcomes).

For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the ROB-GD algorithm (robust shadow scores plus Grover search) with the single parameter rule of proof.md Section 4 (J = max(1, n-2), r1 = 200 bitlength(16(J+1) 10^6), Q = 2^19 (n+4) copies, q = 16 angle bits, p = q + 1 + bitlength(n) phase bits, cosine table of precision 2^-22, threshold 1/400, K = floor(2^{n/2}), k_G = floor(785K/1000) Grover iterations, at most three repetitions) acquires exactly Q(N,s) = 2^19 (n+4) <= 5 * 2^19 n fresh source copies on every execution branch (a deterministic count; the search phase acquires no copies; there are no restarts or aborts), so Q(N,s) = O(n), envelope B_samples(n) = n, whose growth index is exactly 0. This holds on every execution branch, for the clean problem and for every adversary of the error model of the fifth claim, jointly with the other three resource bounds and full-secret success probability at least 49/64 (> 2/3) of the same algorithm and configuration. All constants are absolute (independent of N, s, the adversary and all outcomes).

For the same ROB-GD algorithm and configuration in proof.md, the proved fractional error tolerance is epsilon(n) = 99/100, valid for every N >= 2 (no threshold), under the adaptive dephased-copy model stated in error_model: of the Q = 2^19 (n+4) acquired copies at most floor(99Q/100) are malformed, their positions chosen adaptively by an adversary who knows N, s, the algorithm and all previous measurement outcomes and may use a private quantum system; a malformed copy is arbitrary except that its first (coset) qubit is dephased, i.e. the joint state has no coherence between the |0> and |1> branches of that qubit (its n-qubit register may be entangled with the adversary and with other malformed copies; Regev's bad registers |b,x> are a special case); malformed copies are not entangled with clean copies or the algorithm's workspace; every other copy is, at delivery, an independent ideal coset state in tensor product with everything else, and the adversary cannot act on a copy or on the algorithm's systems after delivery. For every N >= 2, every s in Z/NZ and every such adversary (including the clean problem), the output equals the entire s with probability at least 49/64 > 2/3 (proof.md Theorems 1 and 2, via Lemma M0), jointly with the four resource bounds above, which hold on every execution branch for every adversary. This is not a claim about any larger fraction.

structured.error_model: Adaptive dephased-copy model with fraction epsilon(n). Parameters: N >= 2 is the modulus, s in Z/NZ the secret, n = ceil(log2 N), Q the total number of source copies the algorithm acquires, and epsilon(n) the tolerated malformed fraction. Copies are delivered one at a time in acquisition order j = 1, ..., Q. Before copy j is delivered, an adversary that knows N, s, the full description of the algorithm and every measurement outcome the algorithm obtained before copy j is delivered, and that may hold, process and measure an arbitrary private quantum system, decides adaptively whether copy j is malformed; on every execution branch at most floor(epsilon(n) Q) of the Q acquired copies are malformed. A malformed copy is an (n+1)-qubit system (the register shape of an ideal copy, first qubit A followed by an n-qubit register) supplied from the adversary's system, whose first qubit A is dephased: conditioned on every outcome of every measurement made before its delivery (by the algorithm or the adversary), the joint state of A, the rest of the copy and the adversary's system (including every system the adversary later delivers) is unchanged by the dephasing channel w -> (w + Z_A w Z_A)/2 on A, i.e. it has no |0><1| or |1><0| blocks in A. Apart from this a malformed copy is arbitrary: its n-qubit register may be in any state, entangled with the adversary's system and with other malformed copies, and it may depend on all of the information above. Examples are Regev's bad registers |b, x> with b and x arbitrary, mixtures of them, and coset states whose first qubit has fully decohered with no record of the decoherence retained by the adversary. A malformed copy is in tensor product with clean copies, with the algorithm's workspace and with every qubit the algorithm prepares after its delivery (including the qubits that generate its random bits). Every copy that is not malformed is clean: at the moment of its delivery, a fresh ideal coset state rho_s = (1/N) sum_x |psi_{x,s}><psi_{x,s}| in tensor product with everything else (the adversary's system, all other copies and the algorithm's workspace). The adversary interacts with the algorithm only by supplying copies: it learns the algorithm's measurement outcomes as stated above, but after delivery it cannot act on the copy or on the algorithm's quantum or classical systems. All measurements have countably many outcomes. The algorithm is not told which copies are malformed. Quantifiers: the guarantee must hold for every N >= 2 (no validity threshold), every s in Z/NZ and every such adversary, including the adversary that corrupts nothing (the clean problem): the algorithm outputs the entire s with probability at least 2/3, and the four declared resource bounds hold on every execution branch. The fraction bounds the number of malformed copies among acquired copies; it is not a per-copy corruption probability.
